title: The First Frost
core_theme: The cliché of autumn as a harbinger of decay.
narrative_spec: Write about the exact morning the seasons change. Look at a dead leaf or a cold windowpane. If you rhyme 'leaves' with 'grieves,' I will personally lose my mind.

title: The Post-Mortem of a Tuesday Night
core_theme: The anatomy of modern heartbreak.
narrative_spec: Deconstruct a standard, unglamorous breakup. No sweeping tragic storms or bleeding chests. Just a quiet room after someone leaves. What happens to the air?

title: The Mirror’s Reckoning
core_theme: The realization of aging.
narrative_spec: Look at your own face or hands and recognize a trace of your parents. Examine the terrifying mechanics of becoming your own lineage. Keep it visceral.

title: The Midsummer Suffocation
core_theme: The oppressive weight of peak summer.
narrative_spec: Capture a sweltering July afternoon where the heat feels like a physical entity holding you down. Show me the lethargy of a city or room at 4:00 PM.

title: The Anatomy of Nostalgia
core_theme: The trap of looking back.
narrative_spec: Examine a childhood memory without romanticizing it. Strip out the golden lighting and look at the raw, slightly uncomfortable truth of what was actually happening.

title: The Insomnia Monologue
core_theme: Staring at the ceiling at 3:00 AM.
narrative_spec: Write about the absolute stillness of a bedroom while the rest of the world is unconscious. Is it a sanctuary or a prison? Fixate on a single sound.

title: The First Infatuation
core_theme: The absolute delusion of new love.
narrative_spec: Capture the humiliating, terrifying momentum of falling for someone new. Avoid the word 'spark' or 'fire' entirely. Show me the friction instead.

title: The Ocean's Indifference
core_theme: The classic 'staring at the sea' poem.
narrative_spec: Stand at the edge of a large body of water. Address its scale without sounding like a bad 19th-century romantic poet. What does the tide actually want?

title: The Terminal Diagnosis of a Friend
core_theme: The sudden approach of grief.
narrative_spec: Write about a severe loss or impending departure. Focus heavily on an ordinary, domestic object they left behind on a counter. Let the object hold the weight.

title: The Metaphor of the Open Road
core_theme: The illusion of a fresh start.
narrative_spec: A poem set in a car moving down an empty highway at sunset. Is it freedom, or are you just moving a piece of meat from one destination to another?

title: The Spring Rebirth Truce
core_theme: The cliché of April flowers.
narrative_spec: Look at green shoots breaking through winter soil. Reframe this rebirth without using the word 'hope' or 'beauty.' Make the growth look difficult.

title: The Mid-Thirties Panic Room
core_theme: The quiet terror of settling down.
narrative_spec: Examine the routine of a quiet, stable life. Is the stability a achievement or a slow, comfortable submission to the void? Look at a mortgage or a lawn.

title: The Architecture of Childhood Home
core_theme: Returning to where you grew up.
narrative_spec: Walk through a house you haven't lived in for a decade. Why do the doorways look smaller? Do not get sentimental; keep your boots on.

title: The Train Window Epiphany
core_theme: The melancholy of fleeting transience.
narrative_spec: Watch a stranger through a window as your train or bus pulls away from a platform. You will never see them again. Give that micro-second a pulse.

title: The Solitary Dining Table
core_theme: The absolute baseline of loneliness.
narrative_spec: Eating a completely silent meal alone on a Thursday night. Focus on the mechanics of chewing, the sound of the fork, and the lack of dialogue.

title: The Thunderstorm Protocol
core_theme: The classic summer downpour.
narrative_spec: The sky opens up over a suburban street or city block. Show me the immediate, chaotic retreat of humans looking for cover. GOD I HATE WET SOCKS.

title: The Inheritance of Anger
core_theme: Family conflict over a dinner table.
narrative_spec: A poem about an old, unresolved argument between generations during a holiday meal. Capture the tension hidden inside a polite request to pass the salt.

title: The High Noon Shadow
core_theme: The betrayal of time passing.
narrative_spec: Look at a clock or a shadow at noon. You are older than you were when you started reading this prompt. Make me feel that biological countdown.

title: The First Snowfall
core_theme: The winter blank canvas.
narrative_spec: Write about the quiet that drops over a city when the first heavy snow hits. Focus purely on the acoustic change—the way sound gets swallowed.

title: The Dialectic of the City Skyline
core_theme: The smallness of the individual in the metropolis.
narrative_spec: Look at a dense grid of skyscrapers at night. Millions of windows, millions of routines. Find a way to make this scale feel crushing or liberating.

title: The Midnight Mirror Cry
core_theme: The confrontation of self-loathing.
narrative_spec: A stark poem about looking at yourself after a major personal failure. No metaphors. Just look at the reflection and tell the truth.

title: The Death of a Pet
core_theme: The quiet absence of an animal companion.
narrative_spec: Examine a house that suddenly has no footsteps, no collar tags jingling, or an untouched food bowl. Keep it painfully simple. Don't manipulate my emotions.

title: The Graduation Ceremony Purgatory
core_theme: The terrifying onset of the real world.
narrative_spec: Capture the exact moment a cap is thrown or a diploma is handed over. Underneath the applause, show me the absolute void of 'what happens tomorrow?'

title: The Airport Terminal Reunion
core_theme: The raw performance of greeting someone.
narrative_spec: Watch people coming through the arrival gates. The desperate hugs, the tears, the signs. Is it performance art or genuine human triumph?

title: The Last Walk in the Woods
core_theme: The classic nature walk.
narrative_spec: Go into a forest. Look at a tree. Do not write a postcard. Find something ugly, damp, or rot-infected on the forest floor and center the poem there.
